An alarm you stop by exercising
FitWake alarms don\'t stop with a button.\nYou have to do a set number of squats or push-ups. Moving your body really wakes you up.

1. When the alarm rings, tap 'Start mission'.
2. Stand the phone on the floor or a shelf and step 2–3 m back.
3. Once the camera sees you, counting starts after 3 seconds.
4. Reach your goal and the alarm stops.

The alarm gets quieter during the mission, but gets loud again if you stop moving for a minute.
Camera video never leaves your phone
Exercise recognition runs entirely on your phone. Video is never uploaded or saved, and everything works offline.
Make sure your alarms always ring
If any of these is missing, alarms may ring late or not appear on the lock screen.
You can also do this later from the home screen.
Some phones force-stop apps to save battery, which stops alarms. Please set this up once.
Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → add FitWake to \'Never sleeping apps\'.\nWe also recommend turning off \'Put unused apps to sleep\'.
Xiaomi: Settings → Apps → Manage apps → FitWake → turn on \'Autostart\' and set \'Battery saver\' to \'No restrictions\'.\nLocking FitWake in the recent apps screen also helps.
Huawei/Honor: Settings → Battery → App launch → turn off \'Manage automatically\' for FitWake and enable auto-launch, secondary launch and run in background.
OPPO/realme/OnePlus: Settings → Battery → FitWake → turn on \'Allow background activity\' and allow auto-launch.
vivo: Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management → allow FitWake. Also turn on autostart.
Settings → Apps → FitWake → Battery, then choose \'Unrestricted\' (or \'Don\'t optimize\').
